named_confounds: genre composition change (juvenile/adventure share grows late)
sparse early sample (1,107 works before 1876 vs 5,659 after; some genres have fewer than 60 early works)
annotation/labeling drift in the domain classifier
gradual trend rather than discrete break at cutoff
rationale: Data: 6,766 works, each with exactly one annotated passage (n_passages=1), dated 1800-1925, across 8 genres. Rate = count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages. Estimand: within each genre, mean work rate for works dated 1876 or later minus mean for works dated before 1876, then an unweighted average over the 8 genres. Effect = +0.052 passage-rate units. The 95% CI [0.033, 0.069] comes from 4,000 bootstrap resamples of works, stratified by genre and period. The late rate is higher in all 8 genres, with per-genre differences of about +0.045 to +0.060. Robustness checks: the effect stays positive within each date-confidence tier (high 0.044, medium 0.070, low 0.044) and when low-confidence dates are excluded (0.054). It is also positive within each origin group (UK 0.029, US 0.068, unknown 0.054) and in a narrower 1850-1899 window (0.051). Decade means stay around 0.05 from the 1850s to the 1870s and rise to about 0.10-0.13 from the 1880s on, so this looks like a lasting level change rather than noise. Caveats: the early period is thin, especially before 1850, and some genres have only 37-57 early works, so the early estimates are imprecise. The increase continues gently after 1880, so 1876 may not be a sharp breakpoint. Genre stratification controls for composition across genres but not for mix changes within a genre. Changes in how the classifier labels passages across periods, or in which works were sampled from each period, could also produce or inflate the shift. The cited passage IDs are late passages labeled with the domain at confidence 0.9 or higher, one per genre. They show the construct in use but cannot by themselves establish the trend.
